chapter: Sue and Patsy Howard in show business
title: Buddy Collette as a church singer
summary: Howard says Collette sang in church as a boy and Collette recalls Sue singing at church after he returned from service.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: [PAUSE]

Yeah, it take a lot of time. Did you know, Mrs., that Buddy Collette is one of the prominent musicians in Los Angeles? You don't know it, I know it, but I'm going to tell you. And I can show you books that would be able to show you his name.

Now, there's one thing that I wanted Buddy to do. If you get him to go down to church and sing. He's not going to do this. Get him to go down to the church and sing for you, go down there where they have the bunch, and you'd sure be a happy person, because he's a fine musician. That's the only thing I can say about him. He can play and sing and straighten music out that need to be straightened out.
That's the truth.
I knew that Buddy was a very fine musician. I've been listening to Buddy for more than 25 years, I think. But all the time I've listened I never heard him sing. I didn't know about that.

Well, we'd (inaudible) down to church, when he'd go to church. He was a youngster, then, see, when I'm talking about now, when he was a youngster. Maybe my wife has heard him sing. I'll ask her. Would you ask her for me?
Mrs. Howard? Mrs. Howard? Mrs. Howard?
Mrs. Howard?
Yes?
Mr. Howard wants to know if you've ever heard Buddy sing.
I don't believe I have.
She hasn't heard him.
Well, he has, he sings, he used to sing all the time.
Has he ever sung professional?
No, not professional, no, he's not a professional singer.
Well, he has a very fine voice. That's good to know.
Uh-huh.
That's something that isn't in any of the records anywhere.
Well, he must have caught me when I was quite young. He's right about that, I used to sing in the church.
He did, he sang in the church.
They thought I had a good voice, but (inaudible). But then I had to start playing music and I didn't sing anymore.
That's right, you started to playing music. Used to sing like the dickens. Yeah.
Well, my mother was a good singer.
Oh, yeah, oh, yeah.
She could really sing. So maybe I - (Unintelligible.)
Did you hear the chorus -- Buddy, did you hear the chorus join in?
Yeah.
Susie, did you hear? She knows.

Yeah, I forgot about her singing that one period, when I moved away in the service, and she invited me to church. I played saxophone at this point, I played saxophone solo and she sang and she really -- she got one of those voices that -- it makes you melt away.
